description: The chart is a horizontal bar chart illustrating how many tasks are associated with each linguistic family category. The category axis is vertical, listing (top to bottom) IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque, and the bars appear ordered from highest to lowest task count. The value axis is horizontal and labeled “# tasks,” shown on a linear scale from 0 to 80 with regularly spaced tick marks every 10 units. Each category is represented by a single solid-colored bar: IE-Slavic (light blue) extends to just under 80 (approximately 79–80), IE-Romance (dark blue) reaches just under 50 (about 47), IE-Germanic (light green) reaches the mid-40s (about 44), Uralic (green) reaches about 20, IE-Baltic (pink) reaches just under 20 (about 17), IE-other (red) reaches about 15, IE-Indic (tan) reaches about 10, Semitic (orange) reaches about 8, Turkic (light purple) reaches about 4, and Basque (dark purple) reaches about 3. There is no stacking or grouping within categories, no legend shown, and no bars appear specially emphasized beyond their distinct colors.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of tasks across various linguistic families. The vertical axis lists the categories, including IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque, arranged in descending order of task count. The horizontal axis is labeled '# tasks,' ranging from 0 to 80, with tick marks at intervals of 10. IE-Slavic exhibits the highest number of tasks, approximately 80, followed by IE-Romance at around 60 tasks. IE-Germanic and Uralic show similar task counts, both exceeding 40 tasks. Notably, IE-Baltic demonstrates a sharp decline compared to Uralic, with fewer than 15 tasks. Basque, the smallest category, has fewer than 10 tasks, showing a consistent trend of minimal representation across studies. The chart highlights a steady decrease in task counts from IE-Slavic to IE-Baltic, with a more gradual decline observed among the remaining categories.
